definitions.explanation: A style of cooking where diners grill bite-sized pieces of meat (typically beef) at the table. Often served with various dipping sauces.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Yakiniku came to Japan through Korean cooking. At a {焼肉屋|やきにくや}, diners grill raw slices of meat themselves at the table, then dip them in ⟦タレ→タレ：10500_tare⟧ (a sweet soy-based sauce) or eat them with salt and lemon. Standard orders include カルビ (short rib), ロース (loin), タン (tongue), ハラミ (skirt steak), and ⟦ホルモン→ホルモン：29936_horumon⟧ (offal). {焼肉|やきにく}⟦{食|た}べ{放題|ほうだい}→食べ放題：08291_tabehoudai⟧ (all-you-can-eat yakiniku) restaurants are popular with students and groups.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {焼肉|やきにく}⟦{屋|や}→〜屋：03096_ya⟧: yakiniku restaurant
- {焼肉|やきにく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{食|た}べに⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧: to go out for yakiniku
- {焼肉|やきにく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦タレ→タレ：10500_tare⟧: yakiniku sauce

SIMILAR WORDS:
- バーベキュー: barbecue — usually outdoors, with vegetables and skewers; {焼肉|やきにく} is the table-grill style of restaurants and home hot plates.
